reading.body:
The Independent Community Bankers of America filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports naming AI, making it a repeat filer rather than a one-off commenter.

The pattern is depth of staffing, not breadth of subject. Twenty-two lobbyists appear across those 8 filings, and the same 11 names appear on all 8. That means the ICBA is not assigning AI to a specialist. It is running AI through the same people who carry its other business, which is how a trade association treats an issue that has become permanent rather than novel.

Two bills are named in filings from 2025 or later, HR 2152 and S 2296. The data does not say what either bill would do, what the ICBA argued, or whether the filings concerned AI in banking supervision, fraud, or model risk. A filing records that a client lobbied on an issue, not the position taken.

What this does not cover is the substance. There is no spending figure, no agency named, no outcome, and no indication of whether AI matters to the ICBA because of how banks use it or because of how it is regulated. The count of 8 filings is a measure of attention, not of influence.

summary: INDEPENDENT COMMUNITY BANKERS OF AMERICA filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 19194.
